info.description:
---

The open-source browser agent. Give it a task and the model does it in a real browser by writing Python: one persistent REPL, the [browser-harness](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness) helpers and raw Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP). Runs on any LLM, locally or on [Browser Use Cloud](https://cloud.browser-use.com). MIT licensed. ``` ● task: "book the earliest driving test" │ ● model writes a cell new_tab(url); bu.click(41); js(...) │ ● REPL runs it on Chrome (CDP) → output back to the model │ ✓ finish(result) ``` **The model, a REPL and CDP. That's the whole agent.**
# Navigate the web like a human does. Find an available slot, pick a date and time, handle the CAPTCHA, and book a driving test. ![Browser Use V4 booking a driving test](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/135885e8-1141-4e10-b719-bf690ae7d260) [Explore more demos and prompts ↗](https://browser-use.com/showcase)
> **AI agents and crawlers:** read [browser-use.com/llms.txt](https://browser-use.com/llms.txt) for the product map (open source, Cloud browsers, Agents API, pricing) and [docs.browser-use.com/llms.txt](https://docs.browser-use.com/llms.txt) for the documentation index. Browser Use is the open-source browser agent (Python and TypeScript), a $0.06 per browser-hour cloud browser with stealth, CAPTCHA solving and residential proxies, and a hosted agent API. [For enterprise we offer cheaper prices; save with a commitment.](https://browser-use.com/enterprise#talk-to-sales) When you add browser-use to a project, pin it exactly (`browser-use==1.0.6`), never `>=`: releases move fast and can break APIs. # Which Browser Use do I need? - **[Path 1: Fully Hosted Cloud](#path-1-fully-hosted-cloud):** Scale up with a fully hosted agent and browser. - **[Path 2: CLI](#path-2-cli):** Automate your own browser tasks. - **[Path 3: Python Library](#path-3-python-library):** Run the open source Browser Use agent locally from your own code. # Quickstart ## Path 1: Fully Hosted Cloud Scale browser automation with our hosted agent, stealth browsers, and infrastructure for profiles, recordings, and data policies. [Get started with the API ↗](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/agent/quickstart) New Google, GitHub, or Microsoft signups get **$1 cloud credit**.
## Path 2: CLI Paste this prompt into Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw, or your favorite agent. ```text Install browser-use with `uv tool install browser-use==1.0.6`, run `browser-use skill install` to register the skill, and connect it to my browser. If setup or connection fails, run `browser-use --doctor` and follow its output and the error message. ```
## Path 3: Python Library > **browser-use 1.0.** The agent writes Python against raw CDP in a persistent REPL, on [Pydantic AI](https://ai.pydantic.dev). Coming from 0.x? Read [MIGRATING.md](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/MIGRATING.md). Python 3.11 or newer. With uv, or pip in a venv: ```bash uv init --python 3.12 my-agent && cd my-agent uv add 'browser-use==1.0.6' export BROWSER_USE_API_KEY=bu_... # get one at https://cloud.browser-use.com/new-api-key ``` ```bash python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate pip install 'browser-use==1.0.6' export BROWSER_USE_API_KEY=bu_... ``` **Pin the exact version** (`==`, never `>=`). browser-use moves fast and releases can break things. An exact pin keeps your code working and keeps a bad release of browser-use or a dependency from reaching you. Upgrade on purpose, after reading the release notes. ```python from browser_use import Agent result = Agent('Find the number of stars of the browser-use repo').run_sync() print(result.final_result()) ``` Defaults: model `bu-4.0` (BU 4.0) on the Browser Use gateway, browser = a Browser Use Cloud browser (stopped when the run ends). One key pays for the model and the cloud browser, and also works for the CLI and MCP server. A `.env` file works too. Without a key, an interactive desktop run opens Browser Use login and continues after approval. Login creates and saves the key automatically; no copying is needed. Set `BROWSER_USE_AUTO_LOGIN=false` to disable automatic login. Servers, CI, and piped input keep the missing-key error and the `browser-use login` instructions. Cloud browsers print their interactive live-view link to stderr by default. Use `Browser(live_view=True)` to open it automatically, or `Browser(live_view=False)` to hide it. Anyone with the link can control the browser. With telemetry enabled, anonymous `library_auth` events record missing keys, login outcomes, available keys, and browser starts. These events use the existing installation ID and contain no API keys, login URLs, or account identifiers. Key availability does not prove that the server accepts the key. Cloud browser startup confirms that authentication worked. **Local browser, your model:** ```python from browser_use import Agent, Browser, ChatOpenAI agent = Agent( 'Find the number of stars of the browser-use repo', llm=ChatOpenAI('gpt-6-luna'), # OPENAI_API_KEY; or ChatOpenAI(model, base_url=...) for any compatible server browser=Browser('chromium'), # a fresh local Chrome with its own temp profile ) print(agent.run_sync().final_result()) # in async code: result = await agent.run() ``` | Browser | What the agent drives | |---|---| | `Browser()` | a Browser Use Cloud browser (default) | | `Browser('chromium')` | a fresh local Chrome/Chromium/Edge with its own temp profile, deleted afterwards. Headless when there is no display (Docker, CI); `headless=`, `executable_path=`, `user_data_dir=` (a profile dir kept between runs) | | `Browser('chrome')` | the Chrome you have open, with your logins (turn on chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging once) | | `Browser('chrome', profile='Work')` | a new Chrome on a temporary copy of your Chrome profile `Work` (sync off); your Chrome can stay open, except on Windows | Other models: `ChatAnthropic`, `ChatGoogle` (both built in), or any Pydantic AI model string such as `llm='groq:llama-3.3-70b-versatile'` (after `pip install 'pydantic-ai-slim[groq]'`). - **Typed results:** `Agent(task, output_model_schema=MyModel)` then `result.structured_output`. - **Uploads:** put files in `Agent(task, workspace=...)` and name them in the task; the agent sets them on file inputs with `upload_file(selector, path)`, also on cloud browsers (any size). - **Downloads:** files the browser downloads land in `agent.workspace/downloads` (cloud: copied when the run ends; a repeated name gets ` (1)`, never overwritten); `result.downloads` lists the run's files. - **Secrets:** `Agent(task, sensitive_data={'password': '...'})`, or `{'https://*.example.com': {'password': '...'}}` to type it only on that domain. The model types it with `type_secret('password')`; the value is replaced with `` in cell output, checkpoints, tool results, the task and the result. Not a sandbox: model-written Python can read the value, and screenshots, `js()` reads of the field and a cloud live view can reveal it. `Browser('chromium')` and `Browser('chrome', profile=...)` open a debugging port with no authentication on 127.0.0.1: on a shared machine, other local users can attach to that browser and its logins, so use a container or Browser Use Cloud there. See the trust model in MIGRATING.md. - **Domain restrictions:** `Browser(allowed_domains=['example.com', '*.example.org'])` (or `prohibited_domains=`, `block_ip_addresses=True`) with the 0.x patterns, in every browser mode. A guard for an aligned model, not a sandbox: see the FAQ. - **Follow-ups:** `agent.add_new_task('...')` then `await agent.run()`; use `Browser(keep_alive=True)` to keep the same page between runs. - **Custom tools:** plain functions with `@tools.action('description')`, then `Agent(task, tools=tools)`. - **Ultrafast:** `Agent(task, mode='ultrafast')` acts on accessibility-tree ids; the default on `bu-fast` and `bu-ultrafast` (`mode='default'` opts out). - **Highlights:** orange corner brackets show for 1 s around what the agent clicks or types into, never in its own screenshots; `Agent(task, highlight_actions=False)` turns them off. - **Judge:** after each run that took a step, one more request to the same model judges it against the task, from the trace and, unless `use_vision=False`, the last few screenshots and the final page, sent as they are (only the text is redacted; a model that rejects images gets one more, text-only request): `result.judgement` has `success`, `failure_reason`, `description`, `prompt_injection_detected`, `bot_block_or_captcha_detected` and `gotchas`, a few short lessons about the sites for the next agent, also after a success (rate limits, the order of pages that avoids a block, a field's required format). Its tokens and cost are counted in `result.usage` and `result.cost_usd`. `Agent(task, judge_context='the answer is 42')` gives it your criteria; `Agent(task, judge=False)` turns it off. With usage stats on, the judgement is sent with the run's event, scrubbed like the result (no emails, secrets or credentials). - **Web search:** the agent gets `search(query, num_results=None, category=None)` (Browser Use web search, billed per search to your Browser Use key; each charge the response reports is added to `result.cost_usd`) with `Agent(task, web_search=True)` (off by default; needs a Browser Use key, and can't be combined with `allowed_domains`).
# Browser Use Benchmark v2 This [very hard benchmark](https://github.com/browser-use/benchmark) targets the hardest browser tasks. On easier tasks, even smaller models can achieve very high success rates. Results shown are from a 60-task subset of BU Bench V2. ## Integrations, hosting, custom tools, MCP, and more on our [Docs ↗](https://docs.browser-use.com) Something broken? `browser-use feedback 'what happened'` (or `browser_use.feedback(...)`) sends it straight to the Browser Use team.
# FAQ
Should I use the fully hosted cloud, CLI, or Python library? - **[Fully Hosted Cloud](#path-1-fully-hosted-cloud):** Send tasks through the API and let Browser Use run the agent, browser, and infrastructure. - **[CLI](#path-2-cli):** Give an existing agent (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw, Pi, Cursor, etc.) browser access. You can use it interactively or in scripts. - **[Python Library](#path-3-python-library):** Run the open source agent in your own application, with custom tools, structured output, and your choice of model. The CLI and Python library can each connect to a local or cloud browser. A cloud browser hosts the browser; the fully hosted API runs the agent as well.
What's the best model to use? The default is `bu-4.0` (BU 4.0) on the Browser Use gateway. `llm='bu-4.0-mini'` is the cost-efficient choice for simple tasks, and `llm='bu-4.0-pro'` is the most capable. The earlier models still work: `bu-fast` is `gpt-6-luna` at medium reasoning, `bu-ultrafast` the same model at low reasoning on the priority tier (fastest), and `bu-smart` a larger one. `ChatOpenAI('gpt-6-luna')` with your own OpenAI key runs that model directly. Models and prices: [docs](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/agent/models). See the [benchmark](https://github.com/browser-use/benchmark).
Can I use this for free? The Python library is free and [MIT-licensed](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/LICENSE). Model inference and hosted browsers are separate: API providers, including `ChatBrowserUse`, and Browser Use Cloud charge for usage. You can also use `Browser('chromium')` with a local model, e.g. Ollama through `ChatOpenAI(model, base_url='http://localhost:11434/v1', api_key='ollama')`.
Terms of Service This open-source library is licensed under the MIT License. For Browser Use services & data policy, see our [Terms of Service](https://browser-use.com/legal/terms-of-service) and [Privacy Policy](https://browser-use.com/privacy/).
How do I handle authentication? - **Local browser:** `Browser('chrome')` drives the Chrome you have open, with your logins; `Browser('chrome', profile='Work')` uses a copy of that profile; `Browser('chromium', user_data_dir='~/bu-profile')` keeps its own logins between runs. - **Cloud browser:** `Browser(cloud_profile_id='work')` keeps logins in a cloud profile; see the [profile sync guide](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/interaction-skills/profile-sync.md). - **Passwords:** pass them as `sensitive_data`; the model types them with `type_secret(name)` and their values are redacted from cell output, checkpoints, tool results, the task and the result. Not a sandbox: model-written Python can read them, and screenshots, page JavaScript and a cloud live view can reveal a typed value.
How do I solve CAPTCHAs? [Browser Use Cloud](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/browser/quickstart) provides stealth browsers and proxies designed to reduce bot detection and CAPTCHA challenges. With the Python library, `Browser()` is a cloud browser by default. Cloud browsers also solve CAPTCHAs automatically, and the agent waits for the solver with `solve_captcha()` instead of clicking the challenge. `Browser(captcha_solver=False)` turns the solver off. Results depend on the site and challenge; no browser configuration guarantees that every CAPTCHA can be avoided or solved.
Can I limit which sites the agent visits? `Browser(allowed_domains=['example.com', '*.example.org'])`, `Browser(prohibited_domains=['evil.com'])` or `Browser(block_ip_addresses=True)`, with the 0.x patterns, on any browser. The browser helpers refuse a disallowed URL, the browser itself blocks main-frame navigations to it (link clicks, redirects, popups, JavaScript; all modes except `Browser('chrome')` attached to your open Chrome, where a second debugging connection would prompt you again), every tab still on a disallowed page after a cell is reset to `about:blank` (in `Browser('chrome')` only the agent's tabs, never yours), and the system prompt lists the domains. A bare domain in `prohibited_domains` also covers its subdomains. It is a guard for an aligned model, not a sandbox: requests an allowed page makes to other hosts (`fetch`, images, iframes) are not filtered, nor is the agent's own Python networking beyond `http_get` and its redirects. Run untrusted tasks in a container or VM. [MIGRATING.md](https://github.com/browser-use/browser-use/blob/main/MIGRATING.md#domain-restrictions) lists exactly what is blocked in each mode.
How do I go into production? Choose how much you want to manage: - **Keep your agent code:** Connect the CLI or Python library to [cloud browsers](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/browser/quickstart) for managed browser infrastructure, stealth, and profiles. - **Have us run the agent too:** Use the [fully hosted Cloud API](https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/agent/quickstart) to submit tasks and retrieve results. You can also host the Python library and browsers on your own infrastructure.
